source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
scope: Additive source extraction only. No learner/species.json or photo changes, and no BONAP review.

morphology.habit: Woody-based coarsely pubescent herbaceous perennial, fusiform/woody roots
morphology.leaves: Opposite, petiolate with some auriculate petioles; deltoid, often lobed, serrate blades; stipules toothed and often united
morphology.heads: Solitary on long peduncles; several phyllary series
morphology.rays: 15–30 infertile pistillate rays, yellow to orange-yellow, sometimes purple/red marked beneath
morphology.disks: Perfect fertile florets, yellow-orange, sometimes purple-lined, bases gibbous
morphology.fruits: Flattened, notched and apparently winged cypselae; two short awns usually missing at maturity

qa: Nodal stipules/petiole auricles valuable macro photo targets.

records.original_treatment: Solidago canadensis var. scabra Torr. & A.Gray

morphology.habit: Perennial goldenrod in historical 1999 S. canadensis broad concept
morphology.leaves: The original flora's var. scabra comparison describes usually >0.8 m plants and thin green leaves generally >7 cm long with upper surface less densely hairy than underside; not a species-wide contemporary measurement
morphology.heads: Historical treatment under triangular secund-headed S. canadensis; genus yellow rays and disks
morphology.involucres: 1999 broad S. canadensis 2–5 mm, not independently verified for modern S. altissima

original_names: Solidago canadensis var. scabra (sensu regional flora)
qa: This is a HISTORICAL NAME CROSSWALK ONLY. Do not assert modern S. altissima and S. canadensis are taxonomically synonymous or move var. scabra morphology to modern S. altissima.
Original flora p410 explicitly puts S. altissima in brackets after var. scabra; FNA/modern source needed to finalize concept.

original_treatment.habit: Herbaceous perennial up to 1.5(–2) m, pubescent stems
original_treatment.leaves: Alternate lanceolate, three prominent nerves, hairy on both sides, mostly cauline
original_treatment.heads: Triangular inflorescence, one-sided/secondarily secund heads; involucres 2–5 mm
original_treatment.fruits: Short-hairy ribbed cypselae with many capillary white pappus bristles (genus)
original_treatment.infraspecific: 1999 var. gilvocanescens usually <0.7 m gray-green thick leaves <7 cm; var. scabra >0.8 m thinner green leaves >7 cm; wide intermediates noted

original_names: The flora's broad S. canadensis circumscription includes names now treated differently; do not apply all varieties' traits to modern S. canadensis s.s.

original_treatment.habit: Large herbaceous perennial ≥1.5 m; main stems glabrous, commonly reddish
original_treatment.leaves: Lanceolate, mostly smooth, toothed on much of edge, three strong veins (key)
original_treatment.heads: Broad, triangular panicle with recurved branches, secund yellow heads; involucres about 2.5–4 mm
original_treatment.fruits: Short-hairy ribbed cypselae, white capillary pappus
original_treatment.habitat: Wet or mesic low ground, pond/stream edges, roadsides

original_names: Contrast pubescent primary stems of historical S. canadensis.

records.printed_page_end: Solidago sempervirens L. var. mexicana (L.) Fernald [mentioned, no full treatment]

original_treatment.habit: Genus Solidago perennial, specific habit not documented in 1999 flora
original_treatment.leaves: 1999 comparative note for broad S. sempervirens: glabrous primary stems and leaves; rosette blades linear-lanceolate, stem leaves narrow and entire
original_treatment.heads: Inflorescence racemose/paniculate and pubescent in broad S. sempervirens note
original_treatment.florets: Genus yellow rays and disks, cypsela pappus capillary

original_names: Source NOTE ONLY: p415 authors mention var. mexicana but state seaside forms generally south of their regional study. These characters are not confirmed species-specific for currently recognized S. mexicana.
Requires FNA/POWO modern circumscription before serving to learner.

original_treatment.habit: Herbaceous perennial to 1(–1.3) m, pubescent stems and basal rosette with persistent lower leaves
original_treatment.leaves: Alternate, spatulate and one prominent vein, generally entire, hairy; becoming smaller above
original_treatment.heads: Longer-than-wide secund panicle of yellow heads
original_treatment.varieties: Historical var. longipetiolata: main leaves 7–10× long as wide, involucres 4.5–6.5 mm; var. nemoralis: leaves 3–6× long as wide, involucres 3–4.5 mm

morphology: Solidago nemoralis var. decemflora Fernald [historical variety]
original_names: Existing species record cautions modern split Solidago decemflora; historical variety measurements must not automatically assign to modern S. nemoralis s.s.

original_treatment.leaves: Alternate, rough; small elliptic leaves <1 cm on lower flowering branches
original_treatment.heads: Dense to open panicles with long flower-bearing branches, heads NOT one-sided in field (may appear secund when pressed)

original_names: Unpressed versus pressed head orientation matters; source expressly cautions against herbarium-only secund appearance.

original_treatment.leaves: Mostly ovate to lanceolate, serrate; underleaf with long venal hairs, often wrinkled reticulation and dominant midvein
original_treatment.heads: Triangular recurving panicle with one-sided heads; involucres ~4 mm
original_treatment.habitat: Moist oak-hickory woods, stream banks and roadside ditches
original_treatment.varieties: var. aspera broadly lanceolate/ovate and conspicuously rugose underside; var. rugosa lanceolate with less conspicuous venation

original_names: Variety character should not be assumed for all examples.

original_treatment.habit: Introduced Eurasian taprooted annual, stems 0.1–1(–1.5) m; milky sap
original_treatment.leaves: Alternate, conspicuously stiff and painfully spiny, middle/upper blades clasping with usually rounded auricles
original_treatment.heads: Clusters of all-yellow ligulate florets, narrow green phyllaries in several unequal series
original_treatment.flowers: Corolla tubes longer than ray-like ligules (species); no separate central disk
original_treatment.fruits: Flattened cypsela 2–3 mm with several longitudinal nerves but NO cross wrinkles, white 5–9 mm capillary pappus (genus)

original_names: Compare softer S. oleraceus pointed triangular auricles and transversely wrinkled fruits.
